competencies.text: Explain characteristics of solutions in household products, industry, and environmental science.
Investigate salt's effect on plant growth.

days.title: Solutions & Their Properties
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to define a solution, identify its components, explain concentration and saturation, and describe how solutions appear in everyday life, industry, and the environment.

💧 What Is a Solution?

A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances where the particles are evenly distributed. You can't see the individual components — it looks like one substance.

Solution = Solute + Solvent

TermDefinitionExample
SoluteSubstance that is dissolved (smaller amount)Salt, sugar, CO₂
SolventSubstance that does the dissolving (larger amount)Water, alcohol, oil
SolutionUniform mixture of solute + solventSaltwater, soda, coffee

🌊 Water — The Universal Solvent

Water is called the universal solvent because it dissolves more substances than any other liquid. Its polar nature (positive and negative ends) allows it to pull apart many compounds.

This is why rivers, lakes, and oceans contain dissolved minerals, gases, and salts.

📊 Properties of Solutions

PropertyMeaningExample
HomogeneousUniform throughout — no visible particlesSaltwater, vinegar
TransparentLight passes throughSugar water
Can't be separated by filtrationParticles are too smallSeawater can't be filtered into salt and water
ConcentrationAmount of solute per amount of solventSalty vs. slightly salty soup
SaturationPoint where no more solute can dissolve at a given temperatureSugar stops dissolving in iced tea

🍯 Types of Solutions by State

  • Solid in liquid: Salt water, sugar water
  • Liquid in liquid: Vinegar (acetic acid + water), alcohol + water
  • Gas in liquid: Soda (CO₂ in water), soft drinks
  • Gas in gas: Air (O₂ + N₂ + CO₂)
  • Solid in solid: Alloys (bronze = copper + tin)

🏠 Solutions in Everyday Life

  • Household: Coffee, tea, softdrinks, vinegar, bleach solution, shampoo
  • Industry: Pickling brine, metal plating solutions, pharmaceutical syrups
  • Environment: Seawater (salt + water), acid rain (SO₂ + water), dissolved oxygen in lakes

🌾 Investigating Salt's Effect on Plant Growth

When salt (NaCl) dissolves in soil water, it affects plants in several ways:

  • Osmotic stress: High salt outside the roots pulls water out of the plant instead of in — plants wilt.
  • Nutrient imbalance: Excess Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions block the uptake of essential nutrients like potassium (K⁺).
  • Toxicity: High salt concentrations can damage cell membranes and enzymes.
Salt ConcentrationEffect on Plant
0% (pure water)Normal growth
0.5% (slightly salty)Mild stress — growth slows
2% (moderately salty)Wilting, yellowing leaves
5%+ (very salty)Plant dies

This is why seawater intrusion in coastal farms (from over-pumping groundwater or rising sea levels) is a serious agricultural problem in the Philippines.

🌊 Saltwater Intrusion in the Philippines

Many coastal barangays in La Union, Pangasinan, and other coastal provinces face saltwater intrusion — seawater seeps into freshwater aquifers, making them unusable for farming and drinking.

Causes: Over-extraction of groundwater, rising sea levels due to climate change.

Effects: Reduced rice harvests, sick livestock, salty well water.

📌 Quick Check

  • What is the difference between a solute and a solvent? (Answer: solute is dissolved, solvent does the dissolving)
  • Why is water called the universal solvent? (Answer: it dissolves more substances than any other liquid)
  • What happens to a plant in very salty soil? (Answer: it wilts and may die because water leaves its roots)

days.title: Match Game — Solute & Solvent
days.content:

Match each solution concept or example to its correct description. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Salt in the Environment
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🌾 A coastal farmer notices that his rice plants are turning yellow and wilting, even though he waters them regularly. The well water tastes salty. What is likely happening?

choices.label: A) The plants need more fertilizer
B) Saltwater intrusion is salting the soil — high salt pulls water out of plant roots (osmotic stress)
C) There is too much rainfall
D) The plants are getting too much sunlight

scenario.text: 🥤 You open a cold bottle of soda and see bubbles forming. What type of solution is soda, and what happens when you open it?

choices.label: A) Solid-in-liquid; nothing happens
B) Gas-in-liquid; the pressure drops and dissolved CO₂ escapes as bubbles
C) Liquid-in-liquid; the CO₂ reacts with sugar
D) It is not a solution

scenario.text: 🧂 You stir sugar into hot tea. After a while, adding more sugar no longer dissolves and settles at the bottom. What is this point called?

choices.label: A) Unsaturation
B) Saturation — the solvent can no longer dissolve more solute at that temperature
C) Dilution
D) Precipitation

scenario.text: 🏭 A factory releases hot water containing high salt concentration into a nearby river. What likely happens to the freshwater plants and fish?

choices.label: A) They thrive in saltwater
B) They suffer — high salt causes osmotic stress, damaging cells and reducing biodiversity
C) Nothing changes
D) Salt helps them grow faster

scenario.text: 🌊 Why is saltwater intrusion becoming a bigger problem in Philippine coastal areas?

choices.label: A) Because groundwater is being over-pumped and sea levels are rising due to climate change
B) Because farmers are adding too much salt
C) Because rivers are drying up
D) It's not a problem in the Philippines

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Solutions Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Solutions Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

choices.label: A) A homogeneous mixture of two or more substances
B) A heterogeneous mixture where particles settle at the bottom
C) A pure chemical substance
D) A type of solid only

escape.text: In a sugar-water solution, what is the solute?

choices.label: A) Water
B) Sugar
C) Both sugar and water
D) Neither — it is a pure substance

escape.text: Why is water called the 'universal solvent'?

choices.label: A) Because it dissolves more substances than any other liquid
B) Because it is found everywhere
C) Because it has no charge
D) Because it is denser than other liquids

escape.text: What happens to a plant when it grows in soil with very high salt concentration?

choices.label: A) Water moves out of the plant roots due to osmotic stress, and the plant wilts
B) It grows faster because salt is a nutrient
C) It becomes saltwater-tolerant automatically
D) Nothing changes

escape.text: Which of the following is a GAS-IN-LIQUID solution?

choices.label: A) Soda (softdrink)
B) Saltwater
C) Vinegar
D) Bronze
A) Seawater seeping into freshwater aquifers, making them salty and unusable
B) Adding salt to freshwater for drinking
C) Removing salt from seawater
D) A type of water filtration
